source.title: Essentially No Barriers in Neural Network Energy Landscape
source.authors: Felix Draxler; K. Veschgini; M. Salmhofer; F. Hamprecht

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and Table B.1.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different method—connecting trained minima with AutoNEB—and measures training and test loss and error along the resulting paths. These results bear on generalization behavior but do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures training and test losses and classification error at minima and along paths connecting minima. It does not test random-label memorization, the specified width sweep, CNN-versus-fully-connected comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study measures loss barriers and test performance along constructed paths between trained minima. These results concern mode connectivity, not any listed version. Its width comparisons do not establish generalization beyond zero training error, and its low-loss paths do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find paths connecting independently trained minima with nearly constant training and test loss and slightly increased test error, with barriers generally decreasing as networks become wider and deeper. A single connected low-loss component is their proposed interpretation, rather than a proven characterization of the entire landscape.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses AutoNEB to find low-loss paths between naturally trained minima; it does not reproduce an intervention from the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported barrier trends vary with architecture depth and width and with dataset: CIFAR100 has higher barriers than CIFAR10. Classification-error increases also differ between ResNets and DenseNets.

fits_no_version.finding: Constructed paths between independently trained minima retain low training and test loss, with small reported increases in test classification error on deep architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained image-classification minima can be connected through parameter paths that largely preserve predictive performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing CNN width and especially depth reduces the loss barriers found between minima; deep ResNets and DenseNets have particularly low barriers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional network capacity can permit low-loss connectivity between trained minima.

record.problems: AutoNEB produces upper bounds on saddle losses rather than guaranteed true minimum-energy paths; the authors state they cannot formally characterize the regime. Error bars are omitted from Figure 5, though the appendix reports standard deviations below 10% for values averaged over instances or minibatches.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results were omitted from the extracted text-based aggregate error findings. Table B.1 contains per-architecture values, but its flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of all values to the individual columns and models.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error. The CNN width sweep does not establish that threshold or regime.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the effects of learned locality or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning and recovery recipes.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes. AutoNEB batch choices are not such a comparison.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, varying dropout rates, and varying training-set size.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study disputes a picture of isolated finite-width valleys, but this does not contradict V7's specific correlational claim about magnitude-aware sharpness. Row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; the path-performance findings themselves are reported observations. The supplied table is readable as aligned columns, but its per-architecture findings were already declared in rows_left_out and do not bear on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under the same recipes.
One-hidden-layer ReLU width sweeps past the zero-training-error threshold on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the effects of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Generalization comparisons among adaptive optimizers and SGD under different tuning or recovery recipes.
Large- versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
The effect of adding dropout, including training-set-size and dropout-rate conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
